content: Algarot, also referred to as mercurius vitæ (mercury of life), emetic powder, powder of algaroth, algarel, antimonious oxychloride, or antimony hypochlorite, is a white emetic powder historically used in alchemy. It is composed of a compound of antimony trichloride and antimony trioxide. This substance was employed as an emetic due to its ability to induce violent purging, both through vomiting and diarrhea. Historically, algarot was synthesized using butter of antimony (antimony trichloride). This was essentially the metallic form of antimony, known as the regulus of the mineral, dissolved in acids. The solution was then separated through multiple washings with lukewarm water, which absorbed the acids. The collected washings were evaporated until two-thirds of the liquid had been removed. The remaining substance was a highly acidic solution known as the Spirit of Philosophical Vitriol.
